title: A GA-Optimised Chaotic Key as an Authentication Layer for X25519 Key Exchange on ESP32 IoT Devices
content: Internet of Things (IoT) devices need key agreement that is authenticated, forward-secret and cheap enough to run on a microcontroller. In our earlier work, a genetic-algorithm (GA)-optimised chaotic logistic map was used on an ESP32 to generate AES-256 keys. That study covered only symmetric encryption, and because the generator is deterministic, its output cannot act as a per-session secret. This paper builds a three-layer authenticated key exchange around it. Ed25519 signatures under pinned identity keys authenticate the two nodes, ephemeral X25519 keys seeded from hardware entropy provide session secrecy and forward secrecy, and the chaotic key serves as a pre-shared configuration credential checked with HMAC-SHA256. The session key is derived with HKDF-SHA256 over a transcript hash that covers both messages and both identities, and each side confirms it before the handshake ends. We implemented the protocol with wolfSSL 5.8.4 on two ESP32 DevKit V1 boards communicating over ESP-NOW. All 1,000 hardware handshakes reached confirmed key agreement (95% Clopper–Pearson interval 99.63–100%), the 2,000 ephemeral public keys were all distinct, and all 500 attack attempts across five scenarios were rejected, including every attempt that used chaotic parameters off by 10⁶. A handshake took 3,290.79 ms on average, most of it⁻ spent on Ed25519 verification (748.40 ms), while the chaotic layer added only 0.69 ms. We also describe an entropy-seeding defect in the Arduino build of wolfSSL, which made every “fresh” key identical across devices, and the fix we applied.
